title: A Path That Knows Where It Ends

lines.text: A wait doesn't know where it ends. A path does.
A path is one curve on the field. An auto is a list of steps, and paths are some of them.
First, tell PathPlanner about your robot: its mass, its size, and how hard each wheel can push.
Draw the path from the same tape mark: two meters out, turned forty five degrees. The preview shows the bumpers, so you can see what it'll hit.
Wrap it in an auto, and turn on reset odometry, so the robot starts where the path does.
In code, the drive mechanism tells the library four things: where the robot is, how to reset that, how fast it's moving, and how to drive it.
One autonomous mode registers the named commands, builds the drop down of autos, and reads the choice when the match starts.
On the field, the plan moves ahead, and the robot follows it. When it drifts, a correction pulls it back.
Try it. Shove the robot off the path.
Paths can carry events. In the intake zone, the intake runs, and it stops when the robot leaves.
Three runs of the path land closer together than three runs of the timer. That's the point.
